proved_step:
statement: Let F be any CNF on Boolean variables x_1,...,x_n with clauses C_1,...,C_m; clauses may be empty, tautological, or contain repeated literals. For each j let A_j be the set of assignments falsifying C_j. For S subseteq [m], let V(S) be the variables occurring in the selected clauses, and call S consistent when the simultaneous requirements falsifying every selected clause assign each variable at most one Boolean value. Then |intersection_{j in S} A_j| equals 2^(n-|V(S)|) if S is consistent and 0 otherwise (with the empty intersection for S=empty equal to 2^n). Consequently #SAT(F)=sum_{S subseteq[m]} (-1)^|S| |intersection_{j in S} A_j|.
proof: For each clause C_j, an assignment falsifies it exactly when every literal occurrence is false. A positive occurrence x_i requires x_i=0, and a negative occurrence ¬x_i requires x_i=1. Repeated occurrences repeat a requirement without changing it. If a clause is tautological, it contains both signs of some variable, so its falsification requirements conflict and A_j is empty. For selected clauses S, their intersection is the set of assignments satisfying the union of their falsification requirements. If any variable is required to take both values, this set is empty. Otherwise every variable in V(S) is fixed to one value and each of the other n-|V(S)| variables is free, giving 2^(n-|V(S)|) assignments. For S empty there are no requirements, so the intersection has size 2^n. An assignment satisfies F exactly when it lies outside the union of the A_j. Finite inclusion-exclusion for this union gives the stated sum.

statement: For every finite CNF F on n Boolean variables with clauses C_1,...,C_m, define A_j as the set of assignments falsifying C_j. For S subseteq [m], the intersection of the A_j is empty if the joint falsification requirements conflict; otherwise, if V(S) is the set of variables occurring in selected clauses, its size is 2^(n-|V(S)|). Consequently #SAT(F)=sum_{S subseteq[m]} (-1)^|S| |intersection_{j in S} A_j|.
proof: Each falsified positive literal x_i imposes x_i=0, and each falsified negative literal ¬x_i imposes x_i=1. Thus a conflict makes the joint assignment set empty. If there is no conflict, every variable in V(S) has exactly one prescribed value and the other n-|V(S)| variables are free, giving 2^(n-|V(S)|) assignments; for S empty this is 2^n. An assignment satisfies F iff it lies outside the union of the A_j. Applying finite inclusion-exclusion to that union gives the formula.

lemma: Conditional size-transfer lemma: Let A and B be proof systems for the same unsatisfiable instances F_n. Suppose every B-proof of F_n of size s converts uniformly into an A-proof of F_n of size at most c(n+s)^d, for fixed constants c,d >= 1. If every A-proof of F_n has size greater than L(n), then every B-proof has size greater than (L(n)/c)^(1/d)-n. Proof: for any B-proof of size s, simulation gives an A-proof of size <= c(n+s)^d; hence L(n)<c(n+s)^d, so (L(n)/c)^(1/d)<n+s, and rearrangement gives s>(L(n)/c)^(1/d)-n. This is conditional only and supplies no simulation from general IPS to roABP-IPS_LIN, so it does not close G0003.
